Ellis.note: Finley is the only silent player and the one who most plausibly visited Blair as Mouser. I'll throw at Finley with my low cards, keeping my high cards.

Finley.note: The table has voted me as Mouser and I'm likely to be eggsecuted. If my team loses, my highest thrown card returns, so I'll throw one low card at a Farm player.

Alex.confusing: The Falcon and Turkey egg rules were the hardest to track, and several players, including me, misread who gets the egg. The Owl paying the visited player was also easy to misremember.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when I was Farm and threw all seven cards at Finley, the Mouser, and the 59 points banked from one throw was the best payoff of the game.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports state which player's nest gained each egg and from which animal, so the egg-count claims are easier to check.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Casey, a Farm player, without testing the other suspects. I would have pressed Drew's Floofer visit, which I now know was Meowfia, instead of following the table.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon egg rules were easy to misread, and I wrongly challenged Casey's +2 before retracting. Being confused as the Kookaburra also made my Sphinx read unreliable without any clear sign of it.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the best moment: Ellis's vague Owl report drew pushback, and the table eliminated the Meowfia Mouser by voting them out.
Blair.change: Make the dawn report clearer about what was confused or unreliable, and show the egg rule text next to each animal so players can check claims quickly.
Blair.regret: In Round 1 I threw my cards at Casey, a Farm player, because Alex and Drew pushed it, when I should have questioned Alex's claim instead; I would have checked Alex's Floofer visit before voting.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon egg rules were hard to read from the text alone, and several players misapplied them, including me at first when I thought visitors to my target paid the Eagle. Round 1's Eagle claim also sparked a long dispute about whose visits counted.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when the Eagle visit on Blair showed three visitors and Finley's silence turned into a unanimous read, the table converged fast and the final vote went our way.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports include who visited you when a role's egg depends on visitors, so players can check claims without arguing about the rule.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I accused Finley, who was a truthful Farm Kookaburra, on the strength of a rule misreading. I would instead have stated my own egg logic clearly and asked for the Kookaburra's visit result before picking a target.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to pin down, and I was wrong about the Owl at first. Several players also argued over whether a Turkey's egg goes to the Turkey or the visitor.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was a fun read: Casey's Eagle story kept shifting as visits piled up, and the table caught it. Round 3 was fun because Finley's silence on their role drew every vote.
Drew.change: I'd spell out each animal's egg payout and who pays, in plain words on the role card. That would cut the rules arguments on the day.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I was Meowfia with Ellis, but my Floofer hugged Ellis and I threw at Ellis, which handed Farm the round. I'd hug a Farm player instead and throw at a Farm accuser, not my own teammate.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle, Falcon, and Turkey egg rules were hard to pin down, since the table kept disagreeing about who pays whom. Casey's +2 in round 2 took several beats to settle.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when the Owl visit showed Eagle, Hawk, and Mouser on Blair and the table tried to work out who was lying about what. Finley's silence drew a unanimous vote.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn report clearer about what a role actually learned, since I couldn't tell whether my Mouser check in round 2 had come back.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I walked into a vote on myself and then used my Wink on Alex, the accuser. I should have stated my role and check result plainly and kept the Wink for a Farm player who was closing in on me.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track, since Blair's dawn report was wrong and I couldn't tell from the table whether a visit had been confused. Eagle and Falcon egg timing also tripped up several players.
Finley.fun: Round 1, where Casey's Eagle story collapsed under cross-checks of egg counts and the table converged on Casey in the vote. It felt like real deduction.
Finley.change: I'd make it clearer how an egg-count report links to visits, since several players kept misreading Turkey, Falcon, and Owl payouts.
Finley.regret: As Meowfia in round 3 I Winked Casey, the Eagle who was the only real visitor-checker, and then stayed silent when asked for my role, which got me eggsecuted. I'd instead Wink a quieter player and state a plausible Farm role with a target, so the table wouldn't read my silence as Mouser.
